note: Catalogue capture for the held tier-2 operator manual TM 9-2350-252-10-1 (Fighting Vehicle, Infantry, M2 and Fighting Vehicle, Cavalry, M3; 1982 draft equipment publication). It holds the M2/M3 Bradley as one tracked entry. The manual publishes the combat loaded weight, the engine model and displacement, a gross horsepower rating with no net basis, an automatic hydromechanical transmission, the track type, the track shoe count, the track pitch, an unlabelled track shoe width figure, the maximum road speed, the cruising range and the fording depth. It publishes no overall length, width or height and no ground clearance, so the entry is not runtime-ready and its runtime row states an absent zero for ground clearance. It names no vehicle manufacturer, so maker is recorded as unknown rather than inferred. The track shoe width is the printed 21 in (53.3 cm) value that sits unlabelled directly below Track pitch on printed page 1-8; the row label is absent in the held scan and the state records that caveat. The published centimetre and metre figures are converted to millimetres and the conversion is named in each state, matching the M113A2 and M939 records. No real source maps an AEE game class to the Bradley, so class_token is empty.
